metrics.methodology: Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

write_stages.methodology: Diagnostic SET, WAIT and WAITAOF stages are excluded from logical request and pacing counts. SET latency includes routing, pool/connection initialization and handled redirections before its terminal result; WAIT/WAITAOF latency covers only that attempted command on the same physical connection. Logical set_wait/set_waitaof latency covers the complete write executor operation. Short WAIT or WAITAOF replies have distinct wait_short/waitaof_short classes, separate from client timeout. Unissued commands have no stage latency. Reply histograms exclude errors and malformed replies; WAITAOF histogram keys are canonical local/replicas integer pairs. WAIT replica-memory acknowledgements and WAITAOF local/replica AOF acknowledgements remain separate. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. The period is one second divided by the configured aggregate rate, truncated to whole nanoseconds. A central dispatcher offers only the latest due slot over an unbuffered channel; missed slots, busy workers, stopped tokens, and tokens with no eligible operation are dropped, without catch-up requests. Started requests count actual logical workload GET or write executions; a SET+WAIT/WAITAOF write counts once. Completed requests count their terminal logical metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and ordinary/acknowledgement-policy probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.
workload_stats.guarantee: Every successful client SET acknowledgement is validated, including writes whose subsequent WAIT or WAITAOF returned too few acknowledgements or an error. Every write uses a unique immutable key. SET errors are ambiguous outcomes and may have executed; they are excluded from the acknowledged-write guarantee. WAIT-satisfied and WAITAOF-satisfied subsets are reported separately. WAIT concerns replica memory, while WAITAOF requires observed local and replica AOF counts; neither subset establishes loss-free failover or a power-loss guarantee from this process-crash experiment. Redis asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged writes during failover. This check establishes observed post-experiment readability and value equality, not a general durability guarantee.

methodology: Fault selection preserves the initial primary and its replica. The destructive target is the selected replica; only strictly owned local Docker resources are affected.

Replica faults preserve all original slot owners and do not require promotion. down_duration is a minimum hold from successful fault action completion, bounded by the recovery observation budget. Client service, failure gossip and replication interruption are separately sampled.

Replica network isolation removes its complete bidirectional Docker bridge connectivity while Redis remains running. It is not a selective replication-only partition. Restoration uses the same owned endpoint and unchanged live process identity.

Administrative endpoint-disconnection evidence is separate from Redis INFO link or connected-replica indicators. A short disconnection can finish before TCP/link failure detection; absent interruption or synchronization-counter milestones remain unobserved and are not invented from the Docker interface state.

Crash repair starts the same stopped owned container with its bounded disposable data volume. Redis Cluster identity must match the pre-fault identity. Restart changes the process; it does not simulate power loss, host/storage failure or persistence durability.

The repair deadline covers the restart/reconnect action and subsequent synchronization. Redis's current membership is inspected without issuing CLUSTER REPLICATE or forcing slot ownership. Replica repair preserves original assignments; former-primary repair requires the original replica to retain promoted ownership and the old primary to rejoin as its replica.

Fresh stability after repair requires all six original identities and endpoints, healthy equal slot maps, exactly one synchronized replica per primary, and all-shard client probes. Historical service recovery remains separate from final redundancy and configured acknowledgement-policy availability.

Replication link-up and master_sync_in_progress=0 are sampled indicators, not exact zero lag, bytes preserved, or identification of partial versus full resynchronization. Raw replication INFO is retained for inspection; unobserved milestones remain absent.

Traffic drains before validating every acknowledged immutable SET, including short/error WAIT/WAITAOF outcomes. Ambiguous SET errors remain separate. Cancellation skips unsupported recovery/data claims and still uses fresh bounded restoration and cleanup contexts, including managed volumes.
